planting.note: Cold-stratify seed for several weeks before sowing on the surface of acidic, well-drained mix, since fresh untreated seed germinates slowly and erratically.

directions: This European alpine perennial is the original source of arnica salves and gels used topically for bruises, sprains, and sore joints, and it is the species against which easier-to-grow substitutes like Arnica chamissonis are usually compared. It wants cool summers, acidic soil, and sharp drainage, making raised beds or rock gardens a better fit than a typical warm, humid garden bed. Keep the shallow root zone evenly but lightly moist, since this native of alpine meadows tolerates neither drought nor waterlogging well. Harvest the yellow daisy-like flowerheads for drying and infusing into topical preparations; the plant is for external use only and should never be taken internally.
sources: University of Maryland Medical Center Complementary and Alternative Medicine Guide

planting.note: Start indoors and transplant into warm soil after all frost danger has passed, since basil stalls or rots in cold, wet ground.

directions: Devotion DMR is one of the earlier releases from the Rutgers University basil breeding program's lineup of downy-mildew-resistant Genovese-type basils, bred alongside sibling lines such as Obsession DMR and Passion DMR to keep foliage clean where Peronospora belbahrii routinely ruins older heirloom Genovese strains in humid weather. It forms a slightly more mounding, compact plant than some of its later-released siblings while holding the same classic sweet, clove-free Genovese flavor prized for pesto and fresh cooking. Pinch flower spikes regularly to delay bolting and keep leaf production high, and harvest by cutting stem tips just above a leaf pair to encourage continuous branching through the season. Because it is an open-pollinated strain rather than a hybrid, saved seed breeds reasonably true if plants are isolated from other basil varieties.
sources: Rutgers New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station
